subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw restore cross-machine Chrome extension relay support as a vetted plugin/API-backed browser bridge, or keep the legacy relay retired and require node/remote-CDP based browser control?
rationale: This choice sets a browser-control security boundary and public config/API direction; automation can prove the current gap but cannot choose the long-term relay trust model.

options.title: Design vetted bridge/API
options.body: Add a scoped extension-bridge or browser-backend seam with explicit auth, node scoping, audit logs, config migration rules, docs, and regression proof before accepting implementations.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Close the restoration path intentionally, document why existing-session is host-local, and guide managed hosting providers to node hosts or remote CDP with the required UX tradeoffs.

options.title: Wait for related PRs
options.body: Keep this issue open while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93680 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19289 clarify the minimum safe API surface.

recommendation.title: Design vetted bridge/API
recommendation.body: Add a scoped extension-bridge or browser-backend seam with explicit auth, node scoping, audit logs, config migration rules, docs, and regression proof before accepting implementations.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history for the removal and replacement path is the merged Chrome extension path removal and MCP migration work.
